Planned discharge later today with paracetamol 120 mg syrup every 6 hours as needed and ibuprofen 100 mg syrup every 8 hours as needed. Paediatric orthopaedic review in 1 week to assess the cast and progress.

5.summary: 2-year-old male admitted for elective Ponseti casting for left clubfoot. Family received education on cast care, including keeping it clean and dry, monitoring for swelling, discoloration, odor, pain, skin irritation, or pressure points, and assisting safely with mobility. Gentle exercises for unaffected areas were demonstrated. Continue prescribed oral paracetamol 120 mg every 6 hours as needed and ibuprofen 100 mg every 8 hours as needed. Family instructed to contact the hospital immediately with concerns. Paediatric orthopaedic follow-up planned in one week for cast and treatment assessment.

6.summary: Family meeting with the patient’s mother reviewed post-procedure cast care, including keeping the cast dry and monitoring for swelling, foul odor, or fever. Advised GP follow-up with Dr. Alexander Raymond Mills in 2 weeks for cast review and orthopedic clinic follow-up in 4 weeks for further assessment. Family reported no concerns.

7.summary: Discharge paperwork completed, including procedure summary. Follow-up appointments scheduled, and cast-care instructions provided to the mother. Paracetamol 120 mg/5 mL prescribed as needed for pain.

8.summary:
2-year-old male with congenital left clubfoot (equinovarus deformity), persistent without pain, functional limitation, trauma, infection, or prior surgery. He ambulates independently and was otherwise clinically well; examination showed no swelling or tenderness and no other joint abnormalities. Past history includes prematurity at 34 weeks and resolved developmental dysplasia of the hip. No known allergies.

9.summary: Preoperative assessment on 23/12/2025 for elective Ponseti casting of the left clubfoot under general anaesthesia. Classified ASA II due to prematurity history and deemed fit for general anaesthesia. Parents were counselled regarding anaesthesia. Ferrous sulfate 75 mg once daily was started, with dietary review recommended; no further investigations were required. Proceed as planned.

10.summary: On 23/12/25, informed consent was obtained from Rebecca Stephens, mother of Trevor Antony Stephens, for the planned Ponseti casting procedure for left clubfoot. Risks discussed included skin irritation, pressure sores, and discomfort; questions were answered. No changes to the planned procedure or medications were required. Proceed with the scheduled preoperative checklist.

11.summary: Preoperative assessment for elective Ponseti casting of the left clubfoot, planned for admission on 06/01/26. Consent was obtained on 23/12/25. FBC and U&E were normal; haemoglobin was 10.8 g/dL, consistent with known mild iron-deficiency anaemia treated with oral ferrous sulfate 75 mg once daily. 0.summary: 74-year-old woman presented on 01/01/26 with progressive breathlessness and was visibly short of breath. Triage category 2 (potentially life-threatening). Oxygen was commenced via nasal cannula at 4 L/min and continued to stabilize SpO₂. ED diagnosis: chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. Past history includes hypertension, osteoarthritis, and stage 2 chronic kidney disease; allergy to pollen. Admitted under Dr Pamela Mary Simmons, Respiratory Medicine.

1.summary: At triage on 01/01/26 at 16:20, patient presented with progressive breathlessness and oxygen saturation of 91% on room air, consistent with mild hypoxia. Supplemental oxygen was initiated via nasal cannula (4 L/min at 16:00, then documented as 2 L/min at 16:20) with ongoing monitoring and no adverse reaction noted. Relevant history includes chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, hypertension, osteoarthritis, and mild chronic kidney disease. Triage category was 2 (emergency/potentially life-threatening).

2.summary: At 16:45 on 01/01/2026, arterial blood samples were collected for arterial blood gas analysis and sent to the laboratory to assess oxygenation and acid–base status. ABG, ECG, and chest X-ray results were pending to guide further diagnostic evaluation.

3.summary: 74-year-old woman presented with progressive breathlessness and was visibly short of breath. Oxygen saturation was 91% on room air; supplemental oxygen was given via nasal cannula at 4 L/min, later reduced to 2 L/min to maintain oxygenation. Blood samples were collected for arterial blood gas analysis. Chest radiograph showed mild pulmonary vascular congestion, and ECG demonstrated right heart strain. ED diagnosis was chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. Echocardiography and CTPA were planned to further investigate suspected pulmonary hypertension.

4.summary:
74-year-old woman with hypertension, osteoarthritis, and stage 2 CKD presented with gradually progressive breathlessness over several weeks. She denied chest pain, haemoptysis, syncope, or sudden-onset dyspnoea.

She was visibly dyspnoeic with accessory muscle use, bilateral basal crackles, raised JVP, and bilateral peripheral oedema. Observations: BP 138/85, HR 105, RR 22, temperature 37.1°C, SpO₂ 94% on 2 L/min oxygen via nasal cannula. ABG: PaO₂ 8.7, PaCO₂ 4.6. CXR showed mild pulmonary vascular congestion; ECG demonstrated right heart strain. Blood tests, including coagulation, renal function, and D-dimer, were pending.

Impression was chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. Respiratory HDU accepted the patient. Plan: continue 2 L/min low-flow oxygen, commence apixaban 5 mg twice daily, arrange CTPA and echocardiography, and closely monitor for CTEPH and signs of right heart failure.

5.summary:
Several weeks of progressive breathlessness, initially exertional and now at rest, without chest pain, cough, fever, or haemoptysis. Mild ankle oedema reported. Examination showed mild dyspnoea at rest on 2 L/min oxygen, bilateral basal crackles, mildly elevated JVP, and bilateral peripheral oedema. SpO₂ was 94% on 2 L/min; other observations were stable.

CXR demonstrated mild pulmonary vascular congestion and ECG showed right heart strain. ABG: PaO₂ 9.2 kPa, PaCO₂ 4.5 kPa, pH 7.44. Blood count and renal function were within documented ranges (creatinine 91 µmol/L). CTPA and echocardiography were pending; D-dimer awaited.

Impression: suspected chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension with mild hypoxia and right heart strain. Started apixaban 5 mg twice daily and continued oxygen at 2 L/min. Planned urgent CTPA, echocardiography to assess right ventricular function, and close respiratory/cardiovascular monitoring in the Respiratory HDU.

6.summary: Progressive breathlessness with suspected pulmonary embolism and chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. ECG showed right heart strain and chest X-ray mild pulmonary vascular congestion. The patient remained breathless but stable on oxygen. Observations: HR 88, BP 142/78, RR 20, temperature 36.5°C, SpO₂ 93% on 2 L/min nasal oxygen. Examination showed bilateral basal crackles, tachycardia, and mild bilateral peripheral oedema; no JVP elevation, murmurs, cyanosis, or focal neurological deficits. Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was initiated for therapeutic anticoagulation. Continue oxygen at 2 L/min to maintain SpO₂ >92%; echocardiogram and CTPA planned for the following day to confirm CTEPH.

7.summary: Initial physical therapy mobility assessment completed on 02/01/26. Patient performed seated exercises for circulation and activity tolerance and was taught breathing exercises for exertional shortness of breath. Mobilized with mild exertional SOB without significant oxygen desaturation. Follow-up PT planned to introduce a graded exercise program to improve stamina and mobility.

8.summary: Progressive breathlessness with suspected chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension. Echocardiogram showed significant right ventricular strain consistent with pulmonary hypertension; NT-proBNP was mildly elevated at 900 pg/mL. The patient reported mild exertional shortness of breath without chest pain or worsening symptoms. Observations were stable: HR 85, BP 128/78, RR 18, temperature 36.8°C, and SpO₂ 94% on 2 L/min oxygen. Examination showed bilateral basal crackles and mild peripheral oedema, with no wheeze or acute distress. Apixaban 5 mg twice daily was initiated, oxygen continued at 2 L/min, and CT pulmonary angiography was awaited for confirmation. Specialist pulmonary hypertension team liaison and ongoing monitoring were planned.

9.summary: Dietitian evaluated the patient for fatigue and mild weight loss. Recommended a high-calorie, high-protein diet to support recovery. No medication changes. Re-evaluation planned if symptoms do not improve.

10.summary: OT assessment of dressing, bathing, and meal preparation noted mild fatigue during tasks. Energy-conservation strategies were provided, including pacing and adaptive equipment. Recommended a long-handled reacher and perching stool to support ADLs, with outpatient OT follow-up after discharge.

11.summary: Education provided on pulmonary hypertension, including causes, symptoms, and long-term management. Written materials were given. No treatment changes were made.

12.summary:
Progressive breathlessness due to chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, with CT pulmonary angiography showing segmental perfusion defects in the right and left pulmonary arteries. Mild improvement in shortness of breath with oxygen; no chest pain or new symptoms. On 2 L/min nasal oxygen, SpO₂ 92%; mild work of breathing and JVP distension without wheeze or peripheral oedema. Haemodynamically stable (HR 78, BP 128/78, RR 18, temperature 36.8°C), alert and orientated.

Plan: Start apixaban 10 mg twice daily for 7 days, then 5 mg twice daily; continue oxygen at 2 L/min targeting SpO₂ >92%; refer for right heart catheterisation to assess pulmonary artery pressures and suitability for pulmonary endarterectomy; monitor for deterioration and review the following day.

13.summary: 03/01/26: Physical therapy session focused on diaphragmatic breathing, structured breathing exercises, and gentle stretching to manage exertional dyspnea, improve oxygenation, and promote lung expansion. Patient tolerated treatment well with minimal fatigue. Plan to continue daily physiotherapy to strengthen respiratory muscles and improve endurance. No new medications prescribed.

14.summary: Edward Osborne (next of kin) was contacted by phone and updated on the patient’s condition and treatment plan. He confirmed understanding. No changes were made to the treatment plan.

15.summary: Supportive counselling addressed anxiety and uncertainty related to chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, including long-term management and lifestyle adaptations. The patient engaged well and understood reassurance, coping strategies, and condition-tailored deep-breathing exercises. Referral was made for ongoing psychological support after discharge.

16.summary:
- CTEPH with right ventricular strain, supported by CTPA showing segmental perfusion defects in the right and left pulmonary arteries and BNP 450 pg/mL.  
- Clinically stable with persistent mild exertional breathlessness; mild JVD, bilateral basal crackles, and mild ankle oedema. Observations: HR 78, BP 126/78, RR 18, temperature 36.8°C, SpO₂ 94% on 2 L oxygen.  
- eGFR 62 mL/min/1.73 m².  
- Plan: proceed with right heart catheterisation to assess pulmonary artery pressures and guide therapy; start furosemide 20 mg once daily; continue oxygen to maintain saturations >92%; refer for advanced therapies including pulmonary endarterectomy pending catheterisation results; reassess fluid balance and response to diuresis tomorrow.

17.summary: Cardiology assessed the patient for pulmonary endarterectomy. Based on imaging and clinical findings, the patient was referred to a regional pulmonary endarterectomy center for multidisciplinary team evaluation of surgical candidacy. No immediate changes were made to the current management plan.

18.summary: Physiotherapy session on 04/01/26 focused on graded lower-limb exercises to improve stamina and reduce exertional shortness of breath, including seated leg raises, slow standing marches, and short walking intervals with rest breaks. SpO₂ remained stable at 93–95% on 2 L/min nasal-cannula oxygen. Patient tolerated the session well. Plan to gradually increase exercise intensity over the next two days to improve walking endurance, stamina, and mobility. No medication changes.

19.summary: Contacted next of kin, Edward Osborne, on 04/01/2026 at 16:00 to discuss discharge planning and confirm home support arrangements. No clinical decisions were made.

20.summary: 04/01/26: Occupational therapy provided education on energy conservation, pacing, regular rest breaks, seated meal preparation, and use of assistive devices such as a perching stool for ADLs. Patient was engaged and receptive, with no issues during the session. No changes to medications or therapy plan. Follow-up after discharge recommended to assess implementation.

21.summary: Patient with confirmed chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) due to segmental perfusion defects on CT pulmonary angiogram, with prior mild peripheral oedema, BNP 450 pg/mL, and ECG evidence of right heart strain. Reports mild improvement in breathlessness after physiotherapy and no new symptoms. Observations stable: HR 88, BP 135/78, RR 18, temperature 36.8°C, SpO₂ 94% on 2 L/min oxygen. Alert and comfortable with mild exertional dyspnoea, clear chest, mildly elevated JVP, no new oedema, and satisfactory peripheral perfusion. Right heart catheterisation planned for today to assess pulmonary artery pressures and guide management; no medication changes. Post-procedure review planned, including assessment of suitability for pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA).

22.summary: Dr. Griffiths updated the patient’s GP, Dr. Brown, regarding the diagnosis of chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) and ongoing management. The GP was advised to arrange post-discharge anticoagulation monitoring in primary care. No immediate treatment changes were made.

23.summary: 74-year-old patient admitted with CTEPH underwent a 6-minute walk test and graded walking exercise on 05/01/26. Oxygen saturation remained stable at 93–95% on 2 L/min nasal cannula; mild exertional dyspnea occurred without adverse events. Plan is to continue supervised graded walking twice daily during hospitalization, gradually increasing intensity over the next 2 days, with reassessment in subsequent sessions. No medication changes.

24.summary: MDT meeting reviewed discharge planning and ongoing management, including progress with anticoagulation, physiotherapy, and oxygen therapy. Outpatient pulmonary hypertension clinic follow-up was arranged. Discharge support, including home oxygen requirements, remains to be addressed.

25.summary: Patient with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension reviewed for progressive breathlessness. Reports improved symptoms with less shortness of breath and no new complaints. NT-proBNP decreased to 450 pg/mL from 700 pg/mL on admission; right heart strain remains stable. Observations stable: HR 78, BP 128/75, RR 16, temperature 36.8°C, SpO₂ 94% on 2 L/min nasal cannula. Examination showed normal breath sounds, no peripheral oedema or raised JVP, normal capillary refill, and no neurological deficits. Continue apixaban 5 mg twice daily, trial reduction of oxygen to 1 L/min, and arrange echocardiogram for 07/01/26 to assess improvement before discharge.

26.summary: On 06/01/26 at 10:30, the patient completed a final physical therapy session focused on individualized breathing exercises to optimize oxygenation and manage exertional shortness of breath during daily activities. She demonstrated improved technique and increased confidence in independent symptom management. Advised to continue the prescribed exercises at home using the printed regimen. No medications were started or adjusted.

27.summary: Discharge planning completed. Home support needs were reviewed by nursing and social work. Community services were arranged for post-discharge assistance, with follow-up referral to the community healthcare team.

28.summary: Final occupational therapy session focused on home safety and energy conservation. Discussed removing loose rugs, maintaining clear pathways, and considering use of a walking aid. Demonstrated safe ADLs and recommended a long-handled reacher and perching stool. Reviewed pacing techniques for fatigue management. Patient was receptive and engaged. Outpatient OT follow-up arranged after discharge to assess home modifications and safety.

29.summary: Clinically stable with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension on rivaroxaban, with improved mobility and no new symptoms. INR 1.2 and eGFR 65 mL/min/1.73 m². Observations: HR 84, BP 128/76, RR 18, temperature 36.8°C, SpO₂ 94% on 2 L/min oxygen. Examination showed persistent bilateral basal crackles without wheeze, no peripheral oedema or raised JVP, and no focal neurological deficit. Rivaroxaban is well tolerated without bleeding or adverse effects. No new imaging or ECG performed. Plan for discharge readiness review tomorrow, pulmonary hypertension clinic follow-up in two weeks, and GP discharge communication regarding ongoing anticoagulation monitoring.

30.summary: Final physiotherapy session on 07/01/2026 focused on reviewing mobility exercises and ensuring safe home performance. Patient demonstrated improved stamina and confidence. Advised to continue light walking after discharge, use a pedometer to monitor steps, and gradually increase activity as tolerated. No new medications prescribed.

31.summary: Anticoagulation therapy reviewed. Adherence to warfarin regimen reinforced. Continue enoxaparin 40 mg once daily as bridging therapy until INR is therapeutic. INR monitoring arranged with the GP in 3 days.

32.summary: Final counseling session on 07/01/2026 addressed psychological adjustment to chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension, anxiety management, coping with physical limitations, and adherence to therapy/appointments. Patient expressed relief about discharge and apprehension regarding self-management at home. Relaxation techniques and practical coping strategies were provided; no medication changes. Patient was alert, oriented, engaged, comfortable, and clinically stable without acute distress. She was advised to practice relaxation techniques at home and seek outpatient psychological support after discharge. No further inpatient therapy sessions planned.

33.summary: Patient with confirmed chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTPA showing segmental perfusion defects) reports improved mobility and breathlessness, with no shortness of breath at rest. Comfortable on examination without oedema, raised JVP, abnormal heart sounds, crackles, wheeze, or focal neurological deficits. Observations stable: HR 78, BP 128/82, RR 16, temperature 36.7°C, SpO₂ 96% on room air. Renal function stable (eGFR 65 mL/min/1.73 m²), INR 1.2, and NT-proBNP improved to 450 pg/mL. Planned discharge home today with anticoagulation; plan documents rivaroxaban 20 mg once daily and also warfarin 5 mg once daily with enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously once daily bridging until INR therapeutic. Paracetamol 1 g four times daily as required for musculoskeletal discomfort. Pulmonary hypertension clinic follow-up arranged in 2 weeks, with written discharge and anticoagulation advice.

34.summary: Discharge paperwork provided, including medication changes and follow-up instructions. Patient educated on adherence to rivaroxaban 15 mg twice daily for 21 days, then 20 mg once daily. PH team emergency contact details supplied, with PH clinic follow-up scheduled in 2 weeks.

0.summary: Patient with end-stage osteoarthritis of the right hip, presenting with stiffness, reduced range of motion, and significant pain on movement. No erythema, swelling, or signs of joint infection. Cardiovascular, respiratory, and abdominal examinations were unremarkable. Observations stable: HR 72, BP 126/78, RR 14, temperature 36.8°C, SpO₂ 98%. Mild preoperative anaemia with Hb 10.8 g/dL; U&E and coagulation profile normal. 1.summary: Next of kin, Tomi Fakayode, was contacted at 14:30 and informed that the patient had been admitted and settled into Orthopaedic Ward A2. No clinical decisions were made.

2.summary:
Elective right total hip replacement via posterolateral approach was performed under spinal anaesthesia for end-stage right hip osteoarthritis. Findings showed severe cartilage loss and joint degeneration without significant soft-tissue abnormalities. Degenerated cartilage and femoral head were removed, and a cemented acetabular and femoral prosthesis was implanted. Layered closure and sterile dressing were applied. Estimated blood loss was minimal, with no complications.

Postoperative plan: paracetamol 1 g orally every 6 hours and ibuprofen 400 mg orally every 8 hours as needed for pain; enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously daily for VTE prophylaxis; maintain sterile dressing; cefuroxime 1.5 g IV given at induction; monitor for infection and thromboembolic events. Transfer to Orthopaedic Ward A2, with physiotherapy mobilisation and review planned from 07/01/2026.

3.summary: 26-year-old woman reviewed in PACU at 19:15 following elective total right hip replacement under spinal anaesthesia. Airway patent; breathing spontaneously with RR 14 and SpO₂ 98% on room air. Haemodynamically stable (BP 118/772, HR 76) with no active bleeding. Alert and oriented (GCS 15/15) without neurological deficits. Surgical site intact with clean, dry dressing and no signs of infection or complications. Pain well controlled with IV paracetamol; no nausea or vomiting. Plan for subcutaneous enoxaparin 40 mg daily starting that evening and transfer to Orthopaedic Ward A2 for postoperative care.

4.summary: Postoperative review following right total hip replacement for end-stage osteoarthritis. Pain well controlled with paracetamol; no nausea or dizziness. Patient alert, comfortable, and afebrile with stable observations (HR 78, BP 122/76, RR 16, T 36.8°C, SpO₂ 98%). Wound clean, dry, and intact without infection, swelling, or significant tenderness. No clinical signs of DVT/PE; chest clear, abdomen soft and non-tender, and no peripheral oedema. Hb 105 g/L, consistent with expected postoperative change. Plan: commence physiotherapy for mobilisation and weight-bearing later today; enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously once daily for thromboprophylaxis; paracetamol 1 g orally every 6 hours and ibuprofen 400 mg every 8 hours for analgesia.

5.summary: First postoperative physiotherapy session on 07/01/26 following total right hip replacement. Patient reported mild discomfort but completed exercises successfully, including safe standing, initial weight-bearing on the right leg, and a few assisted steps with a walking frame. Confidence with the frame improved, with good engagement and response to therapy. Plan: daily physiotherapy to progress mobility and strengthen the operated leg. No medication changes.

6.summary: Provided postoperative wound-care education, including infection signs, cleaning techniques, and keeping the wound dry. Reviewed activity restrictions, including avoiding hip flexion beyond 90°. No medication or treatment-plan changes.

7.summary: Postoperative review following right total hip replacement for end-stage right hip osteoarthritis. Patient was well, with stable observations (HR 78, BP 122/76, RR 16, Temp 37.1°C, SpO₂ 98% on room air). Pain was well controlled with paracetamol; mild hip stiffness reported. Surgical site was clean, dry, and healing appropriately without erythema, swelling, or discharge. Hemoglobin had transiently decreased from 12 to 10.5 g/dL, consistent with expected postoperative blood loss. Plan: mobilise as tolerated, continue daily physiotherapy, paracetamol 500 mg PRN, enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously daily for thromboprophylaxis, and repeat blood tests on 08/01/26 to monitor hemoglobin.

8.summary:
OT assessment on 07/01/26 post-THR focused on functional independence with dressing and toileting, home environment, and safety adaptations. No cognitive or communication barriers were identified. Education was provided on safe dressing and transfers and adherence to hip precautions. Recommended equipment included a long-handled grabber, sock aid, bathroom grab rails, and a raised toilet seat. Mild postoperative discomfort was reported and managed with paracetamol 1 g every 6 hours as needed and ibuprofen 400 mg every 8 hours as needed; enoxaparin 40 mg daily continued for VTE prophylaxis.

Patient was alert and oriented, respiratory and haemodynamic status stable, and the surgical wound was clean and dry without signs of infection or complications. Daily OT was planned, with follow-up on 08/01/26 to review adaptations and practise equipment use, alongside physiotherapy liaison for mobility progression and discharge planning.

9.summary: Physiotherapy session on 2026-01-08 focused on stair navigation with handrail support, emphasizing safe technique and weight distribution. Patient demonstrated improved confidence and mobility, with mild but manageable discomfort during stair descent. Continued assisted mobility exercises and stair practice were advised. No new medications prescribed.

10.summary: Postoperative review following total right hip replacement for end-stage right hip osteoarthritis. Patient feels well, with improved confidence during stair practice but mild discomfort on descending; pain controlled with regular paracetamol. Observations stable: HR 78, BP 122/76, RR 16, temperature 37.2°C, SpO₂ 98% on room air. Wound healing well with intact dressing and no redness, swelling, or infection. Mobilising confidently; no focal neurological deficits. Mild preoperative anaemia noted—commence oral ferrous sulfate 200 mg three times daily. Continue physiotherapy for mobility and stiffness. Review for discharge in two days if progress remains satisfactory.

11.summary: Wound dressing changed and wound inspected. No signs of infection or excessive drainage; edges approximated and healing progressing as expected. Continue scheduled dressing changes and monitoring with no change to the wound care plan.

15.summary: Postoperative day 3 following total right hip replacement on 2026-01-06 for end-stage right hip osteoarthritis. 0.summary: 71-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes presented with severe fatigue and shortness of breath. Initial assessment on 04/01/2026 at 18:50 classified him as Triage Category 2 (urgent; immediate attention within 10 minutes), and he was moved to the triage area for urgent observation and further assessment.

1.summary: At 19:15, patient presented with fatigue and was febrile (38.7°C), tachycardic (HR 110 bpm), hypotensive (BP 90/60), and mildly hypoxic (SpO₂ 92% on room air). Flagged for sepsis screening; preparation initiated for fluid resuscitation and blood tests.

2.summary: 71-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes presented to the ED on 04/01/2026 with fatigue and shortness of breath. He was febrile (38.7°C), tachycardic (HR 110), hypotensive (BP 90/60), and mildly hypoxic (SpO₂ 92% on room air). Diagnosed with sepsis secondary to pneumonia. A left forearm IV cannula was inserted and 500 mL normal saline administered for hypotension. Blood tests (FBC, U&E, CRP, lactate, blood cultures) and chest X-ray were ordered. Remained on the respiratory ward.

3.summary: Chest X-ray reviewed, showing right lower lobe consolidation consistent with pneumonia. IV co-amoxiclav 1.2 g every 8 hours was commenced per sepsis protocol.

4.summary:
71-year-old man with hypertension and type 2 diabetes presented with 2 days of worsening fatigue and exertional shortness of breath, feverishness, and reduced appetite. He was lethargic and unwell, with right lower lobe crackles and mild accessory muscle use. Observations: BP 90/60, HR 110, RR 22, temperature 38.7°C, and SpO₂ 92% on room air. CXR showed right lower lobe consolidation; CRP 120 mg/L, WBC 14.6 ×10⁹/L, and lactate 3.2 mmol/L. Blood cultures were taken and are pending.

Impression: sepsis secondary to right lower lobe pneumonia. A 500 mL IV normal saline bolus was given for hypotension; IV co-amoxiclav 1.2 g was started, then changed to IV piperacillin–tazobactam 4.5 g three times daily. Admitted to the respiratory ward for 2 L/min nasal oxygen targeting saturations >94%, monitoring for deterioration or septic shock, repeat lactate and inflammatory markers in 6 hours, and encouragement of oral fluids as tolerated.

5.summary:
Presented with 3 days of worsening fatigue, exertional breathlessness and generalized weakness, with severe fatigue and shortness of breath at rest in the ED. Denied chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, haemoptysis or other focal symptoms. Background of hypertension and type 2 diabetes; no known allergies.

Febrile and hypotensive/tachycardic: HR 108, BP 92/64, RR 22, temperature 38.5°C, SpO₂ 94% on 2 L nasal cannula. Alert but fatigued, with reduced right lower lobe air entry and crackles, mildly cool peripheries and capillary refill 3 seconds; GCS 15 with no focal neurological deficit. Chest X-ray showed right lower lobe consolidation consistent with pneumonia. CRP 220 mg/L, WBC 16 ×10⁹/L and lactate 3.1 mmol/L (initial ED CRP 120 and WBC 14.6). Impression was sepsis secondary to right lower lobe pneumonia. Marginal clinical improvement followed a 500 mL normal saline bolus.

Plan included continuing IV piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g TDS, starting IV co-amoxiclav 1.2 g TDS and IV clarithromycin 50 mg BD, oxygen at 2 L/min titrated to SpO₂ >94%, further 500 mL saline if BP remains <100/60, repeat lactate in 4 hours, sputum culture, and follow-up of blood cultures taken in the ED.

6.summary:

- Fatigued but alert/responsive and haemodynamically stable; right lower lobe crackles without respiratory distress. Skin warm, capillary refill <2 seconds, no cyanosis or peripheral oedema.  
- Observations: HR 108, BP 92/64, RR 22, temperature 38.5°C, SpO₂ 93% on 2 L/min nasal oxygen.  
- CRP 200 mg/L and WBC 14.2 ×10⁹/L. Sputum culture pending; repeat chest X-ray ordered for 06/01/2026.  
- Continue IV piperacillin/tazobactam and refer to physiotherapy for chest physiotherapy.

Haemodynamically stable with BP 92/64 mmHg and HR 108 bpm. Alert and oriented, with mild diaphoresis. Continue chest physiotherapy twice daily, monitor tolerance, and reassess progress.

8.summary: At 11:30, the patient’s next of kin, Margaret Amin, was contacted and updated regarding the patient’s condition and ongoing treatment plan. No changes to management were made.

9.summary: Second physiotherapy session at 14:30 focused on breathing exercises for lung expansion and light bed-to-chair mobility to improve circulation and prevent deconditioning. Patient was cooperative but mildly fatigued. Airway patent; breathing shallow but adequate with SpO₂ 93% on 2 L nasal cannula. Hemodynamically stable (HR 108 bpm, BP 92/64 mmHg), alert and responsive. Crackles noted in the right lower lobe. Continue chest physiotherapy, including percussion and postural drainage, twice daily for pneumonia recovery.

10.summary: Sepsis secondary to pneumonia is improving, with CRP decreased from 180 to 125 mg/L and stable renal function. Patient reports mild fatigue without chest pain or worsening symptoms. Alert, afebrile, and haemodynamically stable (HR 86, BP 118/72, RR 20, T 37.2°C); SpO₂ 94% on 2 L nasal cannula. Persistent right lower-zone crackles noted, with no oedema or focal neurological deficits. Continue IV piperacillin-tazobactam for 48 hours, reassess response and consider de-escalation, and continue chest physiotherapy twice daily.

11.summary: Patient was advised by Nurse Margaret Sarah Holland on DBE for lung function and complication prevention. Hydration was emphasized for pneumonia recovery. No changes were made to medications or treatment plan.

12.summary: Sepsis secondary to pneumonia is improving: CRP decreased from 140 to 65 mg/L, oxygen saturation improved to 95% on room air, and shortness of breath has reduced, though fatigue persists. Examination showed improved right lower lobe air entry with residual crackles; patient was alert, afebrile, haemodynamically stable, and without oedema or focal neurological deficit. Plan: repeat chest X-ray today, step down from IV co-amoxiclav to oral amoxicillin 500 mg QDS for 5 days, continue chest physiotherapy, and monitor clinical improvement.

13.summary: 06/01/26: Physiotherapy session focused on mobilisation and lung expansion. Patient alert, cooperative, and mildly fatigued but tolerated the session well. HR 96 bpm, BP 110/70, adequate perfusion, and no oedema or acute skin changes. SpO₂ was documented as 4% on 2 L nasal cannula pre-session and remained stable at 94% on 2 L post-session. Plan: continue physiotherapy and increase mobilisation intensity in subsequent sessions; no medication changes.

14.summary: Repeat chest X-ray ordered at 13:30 to assess resolution of right lower lobe pneumonia. Results pending to determine whether antibiotic regimen adjustment is needed.

15.summary: Physical therapy session focused on mobilization, strengthening, and breathing exercises for oxygenation and lung expansion. 17.summary: Spouse Margaret Amin was informed of the patient’s progress, including decreased fatigue and increased appetite. No change to the management plan.

18.summary:

Examination: alert and oriented, GCS 15/15, mild photophobia, no focal neurological deficits or signs of trauma/infection. Observations: HR 82, BP 140/90, RR 16, temperature 37.2°C, SpO₂ 98%.
